requirement.evidence: Currently, annual rent increases are capped at either 5% or the Consumer Price Index (CPI) rate, whichever is lower (excluding certain surcharges). However, when a unit has been occupied for three years or more and becomes vacant, landlords can raise the rent by up to 25%—a process known as "partial vacancy decontrol." This increase can only happen once every three years for the same unit.
